title: October inflation at 7.8% as growth nearly stalls
teaser: Cebu Pacific loss nears P13 billion, Building materials prices rise faster, Credit card cash advances to cost more

sections.headline: Prices up 7.8%, growth nearly flat
sections.body: October inflation, the pace at which prices go up, hit 7.8 percent, a 44-month high, writes business columnist Boo Chanco in *PhilStar Business*: [Austerity](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/13/2569708/austerity). He notes the economy grew only 0.1 percent in the third quarter compared with the second, and household spending rose just 0.4 percent. Citing S&P Global Ratings, he says the country is in stagflation, meaning prices climb fast while growth stalls. He lists a 2026 budget deficit projected at 5.4 percent of GDP, roughly P1.66 trillion, and debt servicing, the government's loan payments, projected to rise to P2.704 trillion in 2027. His column is about austerity, or spending cuts and tax increases to shrink a deficit: he argues the government should cut wasteful spending now so harsher terms are not dictated from outside later. That is his view, not a policy. He also notes most government debt is borrowed in pesos, with reserves at $97.4 billion, a four-year low. Not yet known: whether any spending cuts are actually planned.
sections.socialHook: Prices rose 7.8 percent in October, a 44-month high, while the economy barely grew. Here is what the numbers mean for the family budget.
sections.soWhat: With prices rising this fast, the same padala covers less at home; a good week to go over the monthly family budget together.

sections.headline: Cebu Pacific loss nears P13 billion
sections.body: Cebu Pacific's parent, Cebu Air Inc., posted a net loss of P12.84 billion for January to September, against a P9.46-billion profit a year earlier, reports *PhilStar Business*: [Cebu Pacific widens loss to nearly P13 billion](https://www.philstar.com/business/2026/11/13/2569696/cebu-pacific-widens-loss-nearly-p13-billion). *Manila Times Business* puts the loss slightly lower, at P12.78 billion: [Cebu Pacific reports P12.78B Jan-Sept. loss](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/corporate-news/cebu-pacific-reports-p1278b-jan-sept-loss/2468806). More people flew and revenue grew about 10 percent, but expenses grew faster. The Manila Times says fuel costs jumped 62.4 percent to P39.1 billion, which the airline tied to the Feb. 28 escalation of the war in the Middle East, while foreign exchange losses, money lost as the peso weakened, quadrupled to P5.03 billion. PhilStar adds that new airport operator fees raised servicing costs. For families planning a Christmas homecoming, the airline says holiday bookings remain healthy and expects more than 27 million passengers this year, a record. Not in the coverage: whether these losses will mean higher fares.

items.text: CEO Michael Szucs: "The third quarter remained a challenging period, as elevated fuel prices, a weaker peso, and broader macroeconomic pressures continued to affect our operations." *Manila Times Business*: [Cebu Pacific reports P12.78B Jan-Sept. loss](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/corporate-news/cebu-pacific-reports-p1278b-jan-sept-loss/2468806)

*Inquirer Business* also covers the results: [High fuel prices, peso slump ground CebuPac to P12.8-B loss](https://business.inquirer.net/620570/high-fuel-prices-peso-slump-ground-cebupac-to-p12-8-b-loss)

sections.socialHook: Cebu Pacific lost nearly P13 billion in nine months on costly jet fuel and a weak peso. What it says about holiday flights home.
sections.soWhat: Booking a Christmas flight home? Check the full fare and fees on the airline's official site before paying; no fare changes are reported yet.

sections.headline: Building materials prices rise faster
sections.body: Wholesale prices of construction materials in Metro Manila rose 3.7 percent in October from a year earlier, the fastest pace since August 2023, the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) reported, per *BusinessWorld*: [Metro Manila wholesale construction materials price growth in October hits three-year high](https://bworldonline.com/economy/2026/11/12/793593/metro-manila-wholesale-construction-materials-price-growth-in-october-hits-three-year-high/). September's pace was 3.4 percent. The wholesale index tracks what big construction firms pay when buying in bulk. Structural steel led the rise, up 5.2 percent from 3 percent the month before, while cement rose 3.2 percent and sand and gravel 5.5 percent. Lumber, plywood and tiles rose more slowly. The retail index, which follows smaller building projects and do-it-yourself work, held at 2 percent for a third straight month, with electrical materials up 3 percent. For OFWs paying for a house or renovation back home, these are the costs behind the contractor's quote. Not yet clear: whether the faster wholesale increases will reach hardware store prices; the PSA report does not say.
sections.socialHook: Building or fixing a house back home? Steel and cement prices in Metro Manila are rising at the fastest pace in over three years.
sections.soWhat: If your padala funds a house or repair, ask the contractor for an updated written quote, since steel and cement costs are climbing.

sections.headline: Credit card cash advances to cost more
sections.body: The BSP kept the 3 percent monthly cap on credit card finance charges, the interest on unpaid balances, equal to 36 percent a year, reports *Manila Times Business*: [Monthly ceiling for credit card finance charges stays](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/monthly-ceiling-for-credit-card-finance-charges-stays/2468858). But under BSP Circular 1242, the monthly add-on rate ceiling for installment purchases rises to 1.5 percent from 1 percent, and the maximum fee per cash advance goes to P300 from P200. The new ceilings start 15 calendar days after publication and cover only new transactions; existing installment plans keep their agreed terms.

items.text: *Inquirer Business*: [BSP keeps 3% cap on credit card finance charges](https://business.inquirer.net/620498/bsp-keeps-3-cap-on-credit-card-finance-charges)

sections.socialHook: The BSP kept the credit card interest cap but let banks charge more on installments and cash advances. Here is what changes and when.
sections.soWhat: Using a card for cash advances or installments? New deals may cost more once the rules take effect; check your bank's fee notice.

sections.headline: Iba pang balita

items.text: The peso weakened further on Thursday as the US dollar strengthened, and the PSEi, the main stock index, fell 0.57 percent to 5,660.55 after BMI cut its growth forecast, reports *Manila Times Business*: [Peso, PSEi post losses](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/peso-psei-post-losses/2468843). A weaker peso means each dollar sent home converts to more pesos, though prices at home are rising too.

Approved foreign investment pledges reached P336.45 billion in the first nine months of 2026, nearly double last year, with Taiwan the top source in the third quarter, per PSA data in *Manila Times Business*: [PH approved foreign investments hit P336B](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/ph-approved-foreign-investments-hit-p336b/2468753). These are approved commitments, not money already spent.

House Bill 10345 would raise the yearly income tax exemption to P350,000 from P250,000; at P350,000 in taxable income, a worker would save about P15,000 a year. It is still a proposal, not law, per *Manila Times Business*: [Who benefits from the proposed P350K income tax exemption?](https://www.manilatimes.net/2026/11/13/business/top-business/who-benefits-from-the-proposed-p350k-income-tax-exemption/2468816)

The Federation of Free Farmers welcomed the 60-day restriction on some pork imports but questioned why the Department of Agriculture did not act sooner, saying imports have pushed down prices paid to local hog raisers, per *Inquirer Business*: [Farmers question delay in 60-day pork import restriction](https://business.inquirer.net/620543/farmers-question-delay-in-60-day-pork-import-restriction)

sections.socialHook: Also this morning: the peso slips again, foreign investment pledges double, and a proposal to make the first P350,000 of income tax-free.

sections.headline: Noong araw

items.text: On this day, House Speaker Manny Villar passed the articles of impeachment against President Joseph Estrada, a key step in the constitutional process by which officials can be held to account. *Wikipedia*: [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines)

sections.socialHook: Noong araw: on November 13, 2000, the House passed the articles of impeachment against President Joseph Estrada.
